source.title: Video-Text Modeling with Zero-Shot Transfer from Contrastive Captioners
source.authors: Shen Yan; Tao Zhu; Zi-Rui Wang; Yuan Cao; Mi Zhang; Soham Ghosh; Yonghui Wu; Jia-Hui Yu

record.tranche_reason: Reports downstream task scores across model sizes for video models, an extension to the claim's scale-related downstream-performance version. It does not measure language-model pretraining loss or test a loss scaling law.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many video-task and adaptation results, but most do not test a version of the claim. Table 5's downstream results across VideoCoCa model sizes bear on V6. Results in other tables, including adaptor choices, frame counts, tuning methods, and video-data mixtures, do not test the versions' named loss laws or predictions.
record.test_reason: Table 5 reports downstream video-task scores for VideoCoCa (and a CoCa mean-pooling baseline) at three sizes (383M, 787M, 2.1B). This is a weak test of V6 in a video-text setting: it shows only the direction of the change with size. It fits no curve, makes no prediction and relates nothing to pretraining loss. The scaling is a side table in a methods paper, and the size variants also differ in depth and width.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors' main conclusion is that reusing CoCa's attentional poolers on flattened frame tokens gives state-of-the-art zero-shot video classification and retrieval without new modules, and that lightweight LiT tuning gives strong captioning and QA results. On scaling, they note only that VideoCoCa beats CoCa at every size, and that VideoCoCa-L beats the larger CoCa with 3.9x fewer TFLOPs. They draw no conclusion about scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: Tests downstream video-task performance across three model sizes, not held-out language-model cross-entropy loss, parameter/token/compute power-law fits, or fixed-compute allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes are reported by model size and differ by video task and dataset; the paper also reports effects of video-data mixtures and adaptation choices, but those do not test the claim's loss laws.
record.problems: Only three model sizes are reported for the scale comparison; no power-law fitting, extrapolation test, held-out pretraining loss, uncertainty estimates, or loss-based prediction is provided.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5 also reports CoCa scores at three sizes. These CoCa rows were left out to prioritize the 45 VideoCoCa scale-by-metric results; Table 5. Other downstream results are not included because they do not test a claim version's named measure.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss measured against parameters, tokens or compute.
No fits on small runs and no extrapolation.
No shape comparison at a fixed parameter count.
Video models are used, but no power-law loss form is measured.
Whether the improvement is predictable (no fitted trend, no forecast), and the link to pretraining loss. Only three sizes are tested, and they also differ in architecture depth and width.
No analysis of fitting choices or exponents.

missing.what: CoCa baseline scores at three sizes across all 14 metrics. They are mostly monotonic, but MSR-VTT captioning CIDEr drops from 16.5 to 15.9 at the largest size.

record.verdict_notes: Rows r43–r45 are fabricated: Table 5 has no ActivityNet-QA column. All other VideoCoCa values match Table 5. The size axis is the size of the image-text CoCa initialisation; continued pretraining data is fixed (VideoCC3M, one epoch), so this is not a pretraining scaling study. With only three points, predictability cannot be assessed.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run loss-law fits or predictions of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation.
No comparison of depth, width, or architecture effects on held-out pretraining loss.
Video models are studied, but no power-law form for loss is measured in video or another modality or training regime.
The paper reports downstream video-task metrics at three model sizes, but does not fit or evaluate predictions from scale or relate performance to pretraining loss.
No analysis of loss-law fitting choices, fitted exponents, competing laws, or curves bending away from a power law.

relationships.condition: VideoCoCa B/L/full (383M/787M/2.1B), zero-shot classification, retrieval and captioning, and fine-tuned QA, in Table 5
relationships.reason: Every metric rises monotonically with size, though some late gains are small (MSR-VTT R@1 33.9 to 34.3; MSVD-QA 56.2 to 56.9). This shows direction only, not predictability. Rows r01–r42.
relationships.display_finding: Every metric improved monotonically with size, including MSR-VTT R@1 from 33.9 to 34.3 and MSVD-QA from 56.2 to 56.9 at the final size step, without establishing predictability.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: VideoCoCa B/L/full (383M/787M/2.1B), zero-shot classification, retrieval and captioning, and fine-tuned QA, in Table 5
source_check.reason: All fourteen Table 5 metrics increase across the three VideoCoCa sizes. This supports the direction of downstream improvement within the tested scales; predictive fits and extrapolation remain untested.

relationships.condition: CoCa mean-pooling baseline, zero-shot MSR-VTT captioning (CIDEr), in Table 5
relationships.reason: Based on the text, since no row covers the CoCa baseline: CIDEr falls from 16.5 (CoCa-L, 787M) to 15.9 (CoCa, 2.1B), so the gain with size is not uniform across models and tasks.
relationships.display_finding: CIDEr declined from 16.5 for CoCa-L at 787M to 15.9 for CoCa at 2.1B.
